data.title: India's Anand Rathi Wealth invests in property arm
data.description:
Indian wealth manager Anand Rathi Wealth (BSE: 543415) has invested INR450mn ($4.82mn) in debentures issued by sister company Anand Rathi Towers, the company said in a stock exchange filing on November 19. The deal is a related-party transaction. Anand Rathi Towers belongs to the same group, and the listed firm's promoters and group companies are deemed to have an interest in it through their direct and indirect shareholdings.

The target, which until recently operated as Anand Rathi Home Finance, now works in financial activities and real estate. Anand Rathi Wealth said the transaction was carried out on an arm's length basis and in line with the Companies Act, 2013. Anand Rathi Wealth subscribed to 4,500 unsecured, unrated and unlisted Optionally Convertible Debentures (OCDs) through a private placement.

Each has a face value of INR100,000, and the company paid in cash through banking channels. The instruments carry an annual coupon of 7.5%. Holders may convert all or part of the debentures into equity at maturity, or when a call or put option is exercised, under the terms of the issue. Anand Rathi Wealth holds no shares in Anand Rathi Towers at present, and the allotment does not change that immediately.

Any future stake will depend on the conversion ratio. Anand Rathi Towers will use the money for working capital and for buying, building, developing or taking possession of immovable property, now or later, according to the filing. No government or regulatory approval was needed.

The Mumbai-based company was incorporated on October 13, 2022, and operates only in India. It reported total income of INR12.08mn for the 2025-26 financial year, up from INR168,012 in 2024-25. It recorded no income in 2023-24. Its paid-up equity capital stands at INR211.06mn.

data.title: China holds key lending rates steady at record lows for 18th straight month
data.description:
The People's Bank of China (PBoC) left its benchmark lending rates unchanged at record lows for the 18th consecutive month in November 2026, in line with market expectations.

The one-year loan prime rate (LPR) held steady at 3.0%, while the five-year LPR, the reference rate for mortgages, remained at 3.5%.

The rate hold comes despite signs of cooling momentum in October, including softer growth in industrial output and retail sales alongside ongoing declines in home prices.

In its Q3 monetary policy report, the central bank reaffirmed its commitment to an "appropriately loose" monetary stance, signaling flexibility to deploy policy tools as needed to support stable growth without rushing into immediate rate cuts.

Mainland Chinese equities retreated on Friday, whe Shanghai Composite falling 1.5% to 3,524 and the Shenzhen Component tumbling 2.5% to 10,317.

data.title: ICICI Securities' Pankaj Pandey prefers cement and EMS stocks as input costs ease
data.description:
Easing commodity and crude oil prices over the next six to 10 months are expected to drive significant margin expansion across the cement, infrastructure and consumer durable sectors, according to Pankaj Pandey, Head of Retail Research at ICICI Securities.

The air conditioning segment is projected to maintain double-digit growth, having already seen the July-September quarter of 2026 (Q2FY27) demand accelerate by 30% in value and 25% in volume. Refrigerators and washing machines also recorded high-teens growth. While elevated input costs previously constrained aggressive buying, these pressures are subsiding.

"I think the bigger upside probably will be in companies or EMS companies like Amber Enterprises India or PG Electroplast," Pandey noted, explaining that these electronics manufacturing services firms secure price hikes with a lag, positioning them for a stronger recovery as cost pressures ease.

Softer industrial commodities are poised to benefit cement manufacturers directly. Operating margins in the sector could rebound from ₹800 to ₹1,000 per tonne. Combined with an anticipated 8-9% volume growth, cement stocks could deliver returns of 20-25%. Top picks in this space include Ultratech Cement, Shree Cement and JK Cement.

Fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) also offer a margin of safety, with companies like Hindustan Unilever (HUL) trading below 40 times earnings and positioned for double-digit bottom-line growth despite potentially softer top-line figures. ITC and HUL are also highlighted as attractive options.

Infrastructure firms holding fixed-price contracts stand to gain from the commodity correction. Larsen and Toubro (L&T) and KEC International are well-placed, alongside paint manufacturers such as Asian Paints and Indigo Paints.

Capital goods and railway capital expenditure remain robust, with BEML expected to post 30% growth for the rest of the year. In the tyre and auto segments, Apollo Tyres and Hyundai Motor India are preferred picks.

Watch the full conversation here

Beyond commodity beneficiaries, the real estate sector offers strong visibility because construction spans three to four years, insulating developers from short-term material price shocks. Companies such as Lodha Developers and Keystone Realtors (Rustomjee) are guiding for a healthy second half, supported by steady rental revenues.

data.title: JPMorgan says paint companies remain constructive for second half of FY27 - Check top picks
data.description:
Global investment banking firm JPMorgan is positive on paint and adhesive-linked stocks Asian Paints Ltd. and Pidilite Ltd., after it spoke to more than 35 dealers across India to assess the demand trends during the October to November 2026 period.

In its note on Friday, November 20, JPMorgan said demand moderated in November after a healthy offtake in October, due to a shift in the festive season.

It said paint companies remain constructive on the second half of the financial year, supported by a favourable wedding / festive calendar, resilient rural demand and healthy project decimal.

However, the inflationary impact and potential softening rural demand amid weak monsoon remain a key monitorable, JPMorgan said.

JPMorgan added that margins for these paint companies should improve sequentially through the second half of FY27, but still decline on an annual basis, as pricing catches up with earlier raw material inflation, with crude / derivative prices remaining a key monitorable, the firm's note further read.

Asian Paints' second quarter outperformance in comparison to its industry peers highlights its superior on-ground execution, aided by focused interventions and targeted region/market-specific approach, JPMorgan said.

As a result, it reiterated its "overweight" stance on Asian Paints, with a price target of ₹2,665, which is almost the same price at which the stock is currently trading at. Its "overweight" rating on Pidilite comes with a price target of ₹1,635.

Shares of Asian Paints are trading little changed at ₹2,594.7 on Friday. The stock is down 6% so far this year. Shares of Pidilite have recovered from the lows of the day, now trading 1% higher at ₹1,595.4.

data.title: Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest Loads Up $90M In Anthropic Shares, Dumps Nvidia As China Chip Sale Woes Deepen
data.description:
Key points:
  • ARK Invest bought Anthropic shares worth a potential $90 million across six ETFs, led by ARKK’s purchase of 556,777 shares. 
  • ARKQ also bought Anthropic shares while selling 33,430 Nvidia shares. 
  • Nvidia faces a California investigation into whether its chips were illegally sold to China. 

Cathie Wood’s ARK Invest bought around 935,000 shares of newly public Anthropic (ANT) across six funds on Thursday, the day the Claude maker made its Nasdaq debut. The firm also sold 33,430 Nvidia shares from its ARK Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF as the chipmaker’s China exposure draws intensifying regulatory scrutiny.

Anthropic stock tumbled 5% overnight Thursday, after a 17% surge in its debut session. Nvidia stock also traded 1% lower overnight.

Anthropic’s Record Debut And ARK’s Accumulation

ARK’s buying was spread across six funds, led by the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), which bought 556,777 Anthropic shares, the largest single purchase of the day. The ARK Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ) added 90,923 ANT shares and sold 33,430 Nvidia shares.

The ARK Next Generation Internet ETF (ARKW) picked up 146,183 shares, and the ARK Genomic Revolution ETF (ARKG) bought 77,782 shares. The ARK Fintech Innovation ETF (ARKF) added 38,729 shares, and the ARK Space Exploration & Innovation ETF (ARKX) bought 24,574. In total, the purchases totaled a potential $90 million.

ANT stock opened at $111.50 after pricing 980 million shares at $83 each, raising $81.3 billion. That is the largest IPO on record, topping SpaceX’s (SPCX) June debut. At the close, the company’s fully diluted market cap was roughly $1.8 trillion. Its prospectus showed $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up 1,200% year-on-year.

Third-quarter revenue rose 47% sequentially. Anthropic also carries nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Alphabet’s Google.

California Probes Nvidia Over Alleged China Chip Diversion

Nvidia has had a far worse week. California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena on Thursday over whether the company’s advanced chips reached China in violation of U.S. export rules.

The probe follows the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang, who stepped down after admitting to an extramarital affair. The affair involved Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under investigation for allegedly diverting restricted chips to China.

ANT, NVDA Stocks: Retail View 

Retail sentiment around both ANT and NVDA stocks remained ‘extremely bullish’.

A user said, “$ANT Traders will try to front run the additions of the stock to index ETFs and funds, which means the stock may fall once the additions are made and traders exit the stock. That happened with $SPCX.”

Another user said, “$NVDA I will be a buyer on Monday, or perhaps the close Friday. This is way over done. The world needs this technology, nothing anyone says or does or legislates can change that.”

data.title: Palm falls, on track for third weekly decline in four
data.description:
Malaysian palm oil futures fell for a fourth straight session on Friday and were on track for a third weekly decline in four weeks, pressured by weaker soyoil prices.

The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange slid 32 ringgit, or 0.74%, to 4,301 ringgit ($1,046.47) a metric ton by the midday break. The contract has lost 2.11% so far this week.

Palm oil futures remained under pressure following recent losses amid weakening soybean oil, said David Ng, a proprietary trader at trading firm Iceberg X Sdn Bhd.

"We see market direction remaining sensitive to movements in soybean oil and crude oil prices," he said.

Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) fell 0.38%, while its palm oil contract shed 0.53%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were down 0.93%.

Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

Oil prices rose but were set for a weekly decline as concerns over supply disruptions grew following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. O/R

Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.

The ringgit , palm's currency of trade, strengthened 0.02% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly more expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies.

Indonesian state-owned palm plantation company Agrinas Palma Nusantara aims to transfer control of more than 200,000 hectares of land it manages to local cooperatives next year, a company director said.

($1 = 4.1100 ringgit)

data.title: Jensen Huang’s charity pledges $350M to CoreWeave
data.description:
Jensen Huang’s charitable foundation plans to spend $350M renting computing time from CoreWeave , according to its latest tax filing, highlighting the growing financial ties between Nvidia, its customers, and the broader AI industry.

The Jen-Hsun & Lori Huang Foundation disclosed the value of the commitment in its most recent filing. A separate filing by Nvidia in June showed that the funds would go to CoreWeave and that $108.3M had already been spent.

The arrangement underscores concerns about circular financing in the AI industry, where Nvidia and other hardware providers have invested heavily in their own customers, potentially creating artificial demand for their products. Nvidia is a major shareholder in CoreWeave, which Huang publicly defended after its shares slumped amid concerns about its debt-fueled spending on new hardware.

“The Huang Foundation is not a user of the compute; it goes to their grant recipients to do research,” a CoreWeave spokesperson said. A spokesperson for Huang declined to comment.

The program backed by the CoreWeave computing, called the Computing Initiative for Open Science, is “intended to unlock one of the most significant barriers to modern scientific discovery: access to large-scale GPU-computing power,” according to the tax filing.

The $350M commitment is by far the foundation's largest gift last year. Other donations included $19M to the California College of the Arts, $1.2M to the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and $1.05M to College Track, which supports first-generation college students. The foundation also made smaller contributions to the Maui Food Bank, Creekside School and Per Scholas, a Bronx-based nonprofit that provides free IT training.

The foundation's growing charitable commitments come as its assets have surged alongside Nvidia's stock over the past several years. It reported $12.7B in assets as of Dec. 31, 2025, up from $9.2B a year earlier. Nvidia shares accounted for nearly 90% of its year-end assets, while its mutual fund holdings more than doubled to almost $1.3B.

The foundation donated about $373M in total last year, roughly three times its 2024 giving, which was itself double the amount donated in 2023. IRS rules require private foundations to distribute at least 5% of their investment assets annually to charitable causes.

In 2024, most of the foundation's charitable giving went to a donor-advised fund at Schwab Charitable, which was not listed as a recipient in its 2025 filing.

The foundation's financial ties to Nvidia have also come under greater scrutiny following revelations about Huang's personal life. The former CEO was forced out of Nvidia last week after admitting to cheating on his wife, Lori, who serves as the foundation's co-president. He has publicly apologized to his wife and family and appealed to Nvidia's board for reinstatement, but the board rejected his request earlier this week.

Nvidia shares have fallen about 30% since reports first emerged of Huang's alleged affairs, including one involving a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

data.title: Taiwan tells Meta thousands of China-linked accounts seek to influence elections
data.description:
Key points:
  • Meta says it removed fake accounts; no election posts
  • AI-generated videos targeted DPP candidate Puma Shen, Taiwan says
  • China has said it does not interfere in Taiwan's elections

By Yimou Lee

Taiwan has flagged nearly 2,700 social media accounts to Meta that it says appear to be part of a Chinese information warfare campaign seeking to influence elections on the island next week, according to three government officials and internal reports.

In recent weeks, Taiwanese officials identified the accounts on Threads, a text-based Meta platform popular in Taiwan, as suspected vehicles for coordinated Chinese influence operations, according to the officials familiar with the matter and the government reports reviewed by Reuters.

The accounts, almost all of which were opened in the past four months, appeared to have been created in batches and most were identified as Chinese, according to one of the reports.

The November 28 elections for mayors and county chiefs are a key barometer of support for President Lai Ching-te's Democratic Progressive Party — which China calls a "separatist" force and refuses to engage with — ahead of presidential elections in early 2028.

'MAKE PEOPLE TURN AGAINST EACH OTHER'

Taiwanese officials have expressed concern that Beijing, which claims democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, is intensifying online efforts to sway voters before the elections. Taipei rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims.

A Meta spokesperson said the company, which also owns Facebook and Instagram, had removed the accounts flagged by Taiwan's government, many of which had already been disabled by its systems.

None of these "low-quality fake accounts" had posted about election-related topics and most had no followers, the spokesperson said in a statement, adding, "We will continue to take action against accounts that violate our policies."

Taiwanese officials said they had confirmed that some of the accounts had been taken down.

China's Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond to a request for comment. Beijing has long rejected accusations it interferes in Taiwanese elections.

Three Taiwan security officials investigating the matter said the activity formed part of a broader pattern of disinformation, amplification of divisive political narratives and attempts to undermine trust in democracy.

"They don't necessarily ask you to support certain candidates but they make people turn against each other, grow disgusted with democracy, choose not to vote, and they intensify election divisions," said one of the officials, all of whom spoke on condition of the anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter.

An official from Taiwan's National Security Council told Reuters that China had used social media platforms and other means to try to influence the discourse around Taiwan's elections, adding Taipei would continue to work with allies and responsible platforms to ensure elections were not affected by foreign forces.

ACCOUNTS SOUGHT TO DISCOURAGE VOTING, TAIWAN SAYS

Threads is the target of the alleged campaign because of its popularity in Taiwan, officials said, adding that they had not identified similar accounts on Instagram.

Of 2,400 Threads accounts flagged by Taiwan, 74% listed China as their location, while around 25% did not disclose one and 1% listed Russia, according to one government report. It said the accounts fell into 27 clusters using similar Chinese names and different numerical IDs, suggesting they were batch-created.

"The assessment is that this batch of accounts was created in bulk by operators in China or Russia, likely with the aim of influencing Taiwan's 2026 local elections," the report said.

The accounts often sought to build credibility by first posing as ordinary Taiwanese users, sharing posts about everyday interests such as fortune-telling, another official said.

"Then one day, they start by criticising the government and attacking candidates, before saying they are disappointed with the ruling party and will therefore give up voting," the official said.

Taiwan also told Meta that some 260 accounts had disseminated more than 2,150 AI-generated videos that officials say were part of the Chinese campaign, according to the officials and another internal report.

Those videos attracted 2.35 million interactions, including comments and shares, according to the report, which said most of the videos targeted DPP politicians and policies.

That included videos about Puma Shen, the party's high-profile candidate for mayor of Taipei. Some accused him of bullying when he was a student. Shen has denied the allegations.

data.title: Anthropic Defies Tech Rout On Debut — Tom Lee Sees ‘Big Payoff’ Ahead And Says Cisco’s Wild 1997 Ride Shows Why
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic debuted 17% above its IPO price as the Nasdaq fell over 2%. Lee cited Cisco’s 1997 comeback as a reason to stay patient.
  • Anthropic set an $81.3 billion IPO record, but buyers at the open ended the day down 13%.
  • Analyst Ryan Detrick found that 33 of 36 major listings rose on debut, yet the median first-year drop from a peak was 53%.

As Anthropic closed its Wall Street debut 17% above its IPO price on Thursday and the Nasdaq sank over 2%, Fundstrat’s Tom Lee pointed to Cisco’s comeback from its 1997 plunge as a reason for tech investors to stay patient.

Cisco Systems (CSCO) fell from about $9 to $5 in just three months in 1997, Lee told CNBC. A year later, the stock reached $18, doubling the money of investors who had bought at $9 and held through the slide.

“I think that we are at that moment where it feels like max pain, but for the patient investor, this is going to have a big payoff,” Lee said.

Why Anthropic’s Opening Buyers Lost Money

Anthropic (ANT) and its selling shareholders priced 980 million shares at $83 apiece, above the initial range of $70 to $78. The $81.3 billion deal valued the Claude maker at about $1.5 trillion and overtook SpaceX’s (SPCX) $75 billion June offering as the largest IPO on record.

Billionaire tech investor Chamath Palihapitiya flagged a difference between the two debuts. Anthropic opened 34% above its IPO price at $111.50, compared with an opening gain of about 11% for SpaceX. By the closing bell, SpaceX had pulled ahead. It finished its debut 19% above its offer price, while Anthropic closed at $97.17, up 17%.

For investors who bought at the opening price, the difference was bigger. SpaceX buyers ended the day up 7%, while Anthropic buyers were down 13%.

Who Pays For The Next Wave Of AI?

Lee called the tech selloff a healthy correction and said Anthropic could show established companies why they need to upgrade their systems. “It’s a call option on basically the discovery of a lot of future things, and it’s going to expose that existing companies need to rapidly upgrade their infrastructure,” he said.

Anthropic’s own computing and infrastructure costs rose 382% from a year earlier as third-quarter revenue climbed 1,127%. When asked whether cloud providers such as CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) could see higher borrowing costs, Lee said that their customers could help finance the expansion.

“So in other words, I think there’s going to be plenty of people that are going to buy that compute and that capacity, and it may end up being funded by corporations instead of by investors and speculative capital,” Lee said. He even floated a bank as a future cloud provider. “I mean, who knows? JP Morgan might become a neo-cloud, right?”

Lee also said construction jobs could sway the political debate over data centers as newly elected Democrats take office in 2027. “You know, 10 gigawatts in any state is equal to building 450,000 homes,” he said. Without a similar boom in housing, hotels or roads, he said, states would struggle to replace that work. “Losing data centers in any state is a massive economic black hole.”

Tom Lee Warns Against ‘Selling The Lows’

However, Anthropic’s strong debut did little to lift the broader market on Thursday. The Dow fell 2.2%, and the S&P 500 logged its sixth straight loss. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) fell 1.96%, the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) dropped 2.19%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) slid 2.18%.

Lee warned on X that investors who gave up now risked “selling the lows.” He counted 10 previous six-day S&P 500 losing streaks over the past 15 years. In all 10 cases, the index was higher a week later, with an average gain of 2.7% and a median gain of 2.1%. He put the odds of a Friday gain at 70%.

During Lee’s CNBC interview, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) was down more than 8% after Hunterbrook Media reported that a Chinese server maker on a U.S. export blacklist had used updated AMD firmware. “The claims misrepresent AMD’s business practices and relationships,” an AMD spokesperson told Reuters. The company said it complies with U.S. export controls. Hunterbrook’s affiliated hedge fund disclosed a short position in AMD.

When asked whether AMD’s slide reflected broader unease after Nvidia’s (NVDA) recent disclosures, Lee said there were limits to what chip restrictions could achieve. “Because you know, if we limit hardware, we can’t necessarily limit software,” he said. He expects AI to remain a major market story in 2027. “I think that this is an important reset, and I think next year it’s still going to be one of the biggest stories.”

Analyst: The Day-1 Pop Can Fade Fast

On the other hand, Carson Group’s chief market strategist Ryan Detrick offered a reason to be patient about buying Anthropic. Of 36 major listings he tracked since Google’s 2004 debut, 33 rose on day one. The median first-day gain was 31.2%, yet the median drop from a first-year peak was 52.6%. Figma (FIG) showed how quickly fortunes could turn. Its shares soared 250% on debut and later fell 86.2% from a peak.

“Looking at previous major IPOs shows that a pop on Day 1 is common. But so is a massive correction at some point over the next year,” Detrick said.

Futurum Group CEO Daniel Newman also saw room for optimism about AI and patience on Anthropic’s share price. “AI sentiment is in the gutter, but today’s IPO has a chance to shift momentum,” he said before trading began. For investors who missed the debut, he pointed to a broader pattern: IPOs gain about 19% on average on day one, he said, but 60% trade lower a year later.

Gordon Johnson Sees Echoes Of Dot-Com Bust

While Lee sees a parallel with Cisco’s 1997 comeback, GLJ Research analyst Gordon Johnson sees one with the 2000 tech bust, when a flood of new shares competed for investors’ cash.

Johnson tallied more than $700 billion across the AI sector this year. It includes $156 billion from the Anthropic and SpaceX IPOs, about $180 billion in announced equity programs at Alphabet (GOOG) and Meta Platforms (META), and more than $370 billion in bonds from major cloud companies. Some of those stock sales could still lie ahead. Alphabet’s plan allows it to sell up to $40 billion in shares over time, while Meta’s $97.5 billion plan includes up to $60 billion in such sales.

Johnson sees another test when IPO lockups expire, freeing employees and early backers to sell. His concern is whether enough buyers will be waiting. “The AI revolution is real. So is the wall of paper,” he said.

data.title: Alibaba reportedly sued over Megaspeed ties amid Nvidia spy scandal
data.description:
Alibaba is said to have been sued by shareholders in New York on Thursday, with investors alleging that the Chinese e-commerce giant misled them by concealing its connections to a suspected Chinese spy whose links to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang reportedly contributed to his resignation last week.

According to a ​proposed class action filed in Manhattan federal court, Alibaba inflated its share price by knowingly ​and materially understating in its 2024, 2025, and 2026 annual reports the risks that ⁠actual or suspected export control violations could harm its business, Reuters reported.

Shareholders cited Alibaba's relationship with Megaspeed, a ​Singaporean company suspected of helping Beijing gain access to advanced Nvidia AI chips, and whose executive Alice Huang ​had a relationship with Jensen Huang, who is not related to her.

The shareholders said Alibaba shares fell 14% over four days last week because of media reports on Alibaba's ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed, including that Alibaba had ​become Megaspeed's “dominant” customer, the report said.

Nvidia itself faces several shareholder lawsuits over the spy scandal, including allegations of lax oversight by its directors.

The e-commerce giant's CEO Eddie Wu said on Thursday that Alibaba remained on track for $100B in external cloud revenue and a 20% EBITDA margin by 2030, despite U.S. curbs on ​access to computing power that ​could affect the company's ⁠products and services next year. The restrictions were imposed after Huang resigned from Nvidia.

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, along with ​her husband and sister, built a network of companies across ⁠China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, The Information has reported previously.

When orders for Nvidia chips subject to U.S. export restrictions  stalled, Alice Huang used ties to Nvidia to secure supplies, helping move about 240,000 H100, H200 and some A100 chips into China, according to the report. data.title: Japan's October core CPI rises to 2.2%, misses estimates, and headline inflation hits 11-month high
data.description:
Japan’s annual inflation rate accelerated to 2.3% in October 2026 from 2.1% in September, reaching its highest level since November 2025. On a monthly basis, consumer prices increased 0.5%, up from 0.4% in the prior month and marking the steepest monthly gain since December 2024.

The core consumer price index (excluding fresh food) rose 2.2% Y/Y, up from 2.1% in September to hit its highest reading since December 2025, though slightly below forecasts of 2.3%.

The "core-core" index (excluding both fresh food and energy), closely monitored by the Bank of Japan, eased to 2.2% Y/Y from September's six-month high of 2.4%.

Food inflation slowed to 2.7% from 3.8%, marking its slowest pace since January 2022.

On Friday, the benchmark Nikkei 225 Index plunged more than 4% to below the 57,000 mark on Friday. Meanwhile, the Japanese yen appreciated toward 159 per dollar on Friday, recovering from losses in the previous session.

data.title: HSBC is betting on this new listing for an upside of 47%
data.description:
Shares of OnEMI Technology Solutions Ltd., the parent company of digital lending platform Kissht, were trading over 4% higher on Friday, November 20, after global brokerage HSBC initiated coverage on the stock with a 'Buy' rating.

HSBC has set a price target of ₹500 per share. The target implies an upside of about 47% from the stock's closing price on Thursday (November 19).

According to HSBC, Kissht is among a select group of Indian companies with a differentiated business model focused on digital unsecured lending. The brokerage expects the company to deliver strong earnings growth over the next few years, supported by rapid expansion from a relatively small base, improving operating efficiencies and disciplined credit costs.

HSBC estimates that these factors could help OnEMI Technology clock a profit after tax (PAT) compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of around 60% over FY26-FY29.

The brokerage also sees the stock as attractively valued, trading at an implied price-to-book (P/B) multiple of 2.2 times its estimated FY28 book value per share (BVPS).

The positive outlook follows a strong second quarter for the company. Kissht's assets under management (AUM) increased 68% year-on-year to ₹9,317 crore in Q2FY27, while its net profit doubled to ₹125 crore. Gross non-performing assets (GNPA) stood at 2.18%.

The company has also raised its AUM growth guidance for FY27 to more than 60%, reflecting confidence in its lending business and growth momentum.

With HSBC's initiation, all three analysts tracking the stock have a 'Buy' recommendation, according to the available analyst coverage data.

OnEMI Technology made its Dalal Street debut earlier in May this year. The stock had opened at ₹191 on the BSE and at ₹190 on the NSE.

Founded in 2016, OnEMI Technology Solutions operates as a technology-driven lending platform focused on consumer and MSME financing.

The company runs lending platforms such as Kissht and Ring, which offer EMI-based credit solutions across online and offline merchant networks. Its NBFC arm, Si Creva Capital Services, manages underwriting, loan disbursement, KYC processes and collections.

data.title: China's October soybean imports fall 23% as Brazil shipments decline
data.description:
China's soybean imports from Brazil fell 7% in October from a year earlier, contributing to a 23% drop in the country's overall soybean arrivals, data from the General Administration of Customs showed on Friday.

Imports from Brazil slipped to 6.6 million metric tons last month, down 38% from September.

  • China, the world's largest soybean buyer, imported 7.3 million tons of soybeans in October

  • US shipments also remained subdued. Imports from the US stood at 0.18 million tons in October, up from zero a year earlier but down 56% from September

  • For January-October, soybean imports from the U.S. fell 33% from a year earlier to 11.3 million tons, while shipments from Brazil rose 2.3% to 72.5 million tons

  • Trade tensions between Beijing and Washington last year prompted Chinese buyers to delay purchases of US soybeans until after an October summit between the two countries' leaders

  • Following the meeting, China purchased around 12 million tons of US soybeans, though that remained well below pre-trade-war levels

  • China had also purchased more than 60% of its 25-million-ton US soybean buying target for the 2026/27 marketing year, with shipments beginning in September, traders told Reuters last week

data.title: Trip.Best Unveils Its Biggest Global Rankings Yet, Covering All Seven Continents for the First Time
data.description:
Global travel rankings grow to 98 annual lists across nine regions and 22 languages, with the first standalone Oceania lists.

SYDNEY, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Trip.Best, the global travel rankings from Trip.com Group, launched its 2027 Annual Rankings in Sydney, extending coverage to all seven continents for the first time. Unveiled at The Dome, Sydney Showground, as part of Trip.com Group's Global Partner Summit, this year's edition grows from 85 to 98 annual rankings and from five to nine regions, across 22 languages.

Oceania, Africa and Antarctica join as new regions, and the Americas are now split into North and South America. In total, the 2027 Annual Rankings feature more than 3,700 entries across 112 countries and regions, spanning hotels, attractions, nightlife, dining and destinations. Winners were recognised at the Global 100 Awards Ceremony.

Oceania Steps Into the Global Spotlight With Eight Standalone Rankings

For the first time, Trip.Best publishes eight standalone Oceania 50 lists, recognising more than 250 hotels, attractions, restaurants and experiences across Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands. The lists cover scenic hotels, must-see and family attractions, nightlife, fine dining and must-visit restaurants, with ski-resort and hot-spring rankings reflecting the region's year-round appeal.

Top-ranked winners include:

  • Scenic Hotel: Four Seasons Resort Bora Bora, followed by Park Hyatt Sydney and Rosewood Kauri Cliffs in New Zealand.
  • Best Things to Do: Sydney Opera House, followed by Bora Bora and the TSS Earnslaw Steamship in Queenstown.
  • Fine Dining: Essence in Queenstown, followed by Bennelong in Sydney and Jano Bistro in Wellington.
  • Must-Visit Restaurant: Fergburger in Queenstown, followed by Bar Totti's in Sydney and Depot in Auckland.

Global 100 Lists Honour Leading Hotels, Sights and Restaurants

At global level, the Global 100 lists are led by:

  • Luxury Hotel: Hôtel de Crillon, A Rosewood Hotel in Paris, followed by Raffles Singapore and Le Bristol Paris.
  • Scenic Hotel: Il San Pietro di Positano in Italy, followed by Cheval Blanc Randheli in the Maldives and Le Sirenuse in Positano.
  • Best Things to Do: The Louvre in Paris.
  • Fine Dining: DiverXO in Madrid, followed by L'Arpège in Paris and Disfrutar in Barcelona.

New Wonders Lists Showcase What Makes a Destination Distinctive

Trip.Best also introduces Wonders - a new collection of rankings aimed at international travellers seeking inspiration for their next destination. Each list is built on what makes a destination distinctive and what gives it an edge over others across markets. The collection comprises 49 themed lists across 10 countries and four categories (hotels, attractions, food and destinations) and is available in 22 languages.

Australia features in two lists: Native Wildlife Conservation Encounters, led by Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary, and Outdoor Adventures, led by Cairns. Global Wonders lists include Diving Experiences, Ski Towns and Sunset Views.

data.title: Corpay, TPG To Buy BILL Holdings For $6 Bln
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Corpay, Inc. (CPAY), a payments and spend management company, said that it has inked a deal to make a $1.1 billion minority investment in BILL Holdings, Inc. (BILL) as part of a transaction to take BILL private alongside TPG Inc. (TPG) for $63.25 per share that values BILL at $6 billion.

Under the terms, Corpay will invest $1.1 billion for around a one-third equity stake in the company with the option to acquire all shares of the company. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

Peter Walker, CFO of Corpay, said: 'We expect the transaction to be accretive to Corpay cash EPS in 2027, and the take-private transaction structure gives the company the flexibility to transform and accelerate profit growth. We have the option to buy the rest of the company in 2030.'
